newsitem.title: MEXICO: GSyR says to pay debt with shopping malls.
newsitem.headline: GSyR says to pay debt with shopping malls.

text.p: Troubled Mexican retailer Grupo Salinas y Rocha (GSyR) plans to include two major Mexico City shopping malls as payment in kind to creditors as part of a financial restructuring program, a company executive said on Tuesday.

"We cannot give many details until the agreement is signed, but obviously among the set of assets we have which are easier to manage in payment are shopping malls," GSyR Chief Financial Officer Tomas Valladares said in a telephone interview.
"Shopping centers such as those at Perisur and Santa Fe, which we own, are those we would give in payment," Valladares added.
Valladares said GSyR intends to pay off close to $500 million of debt in the coming days, which analysts estimate to be one-quarter of the group's total outstanding debt.
Valladares denied newspaper reports that a memorandum of understanding between GSyR and creditor banks would be signed on Tuesday and said this would not take place until the end of April.
"We have a news conference planned for April 25 and hope by that date to have a financial restructuring agreement signed and first-quarter results formally posted," Valladares said.

Valladares also denied stock market rumors the firm was planning an asset sale, such as the recent sale by Sears, Roebuck, Co of a 60-percent stake in its Mexican subsidiary to conglomerate Grupo Carso.
